title: Children's prayers
tomorrow: Chicago's group chats are forming. who will Amira sit with?

segments.voice: Yesterday, keep the tie: one soul at the root of us all, and kin down the hall. The week's last stop is the smallest people in the house.

A toddler in a living room waits until a grown-up goes down into prostration, forehead on the floor, and then climbs on like it's a jungle gym. Now what? It happened to the Prophet ﷺ. In a report in Sunan an-Nasa'i, he stays down in one prostration so long that the people praying behind him wonder if something has happened. Afterward he explains: my son was riding on my back, and I didn't want to rush him.
screen: `A CHILD CLIMBS ON.` → `HE STAYS DOWN.` → `I DIDN'T WANT TO RUSH HIM.`

segments.voice: It was his grandson, in fact, and he called him my son. Another report, in Sahih al-Bukhari, has him leading prayer while carrying his granddaughter Umamah: he set her down to prostrate, and picked her up again when he stood. In these reports children aren't kept away from prayer. They're on its back and in its arms. Praying together isn't a lecture about prayer; it's prayer with a small person in it. The Qur'an gives words for the other half, praying for them, from Abraham. In Pickthall's words: "My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also)." Now the week, quickly. A trench, and a leader carrying earth: generous at work. A man told to sleep: the body's right. Birds that leave the nest: provision is written. A sandal mended: mercy at home. A door down the hall: the middle door. A psalm and a single soul: keep the tie. Six days, a house filling up, and today a child on a back and a grown-up who waits.
screen: `HE CALLED HIM MY SON.` · `UMAMAH IN HIS ARMS.` · `ABRAHAM: AND MY CHILDREN TOO.` · `A WEEK, A HOUSE FILLING UP.` · then, large: `PRAY TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind the person who first taught you a word worth keeping, a prayer, a blessing, a thank-you. Say that word aloud, slowly, the way a child learns it, one sound at a time. Then sit with whoever taught it to you in mind, and whoever you might teach it to next.
screen: `THE FIRST WORD YOU WERE TAUGHT.` · `ALOUD, ONE SOUND AT A TIME.`

segments.voice: Children's prayers: praying with children, and for them. The Prophet stayed down so a child could finish his ride.
Last line of the week: pray together, with a child on your back if need be. Four of ten, and a full week.

howItsDone: Muslim families pray together at home with children standing beside them, and children come along to the masjid; a parent may pray with a little one nearby, and parents ask God for their children in their own prayers.
